record.file_problem: Repository metadata and README only; code and result files were not read or run.
record.tranche_reason: The README reports removal of refusals with a runtime rank-1 projection on a new model. The direction is extracted from checkpoint weight differences, not by the original difference-in-mean-activations method.
record.gate_note: The README reports refusal, capability, and spectral-probe outcomes. Direction-selection values and implementation tests are not behavioral results. The baked checkpoint is discussed through edit magnitude and acceptance, but no baked-checkpoint refusal rate is reported. No result tests adding the direction to induce refusals on harmless requests.
record.test_reason: The study ablates the abliteration direction at runtime on a new model, the MoE reasoning model DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731. It reports refusal rates across λ plus capability checks, so its own results bear on V1 and V8. The direction is the published abliteration edit recovered by SVD of the weight difference, not a fresh harmful-minus-harmless extraction. It is a new setting with a result on the claim rather than a new method for the same question.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The README concludes that runtime rank-1 projection removes refusal on its 10-trigger set, saturating at λ=1.5. At λ=1.5 it reports no measurable cost on acceptance, NIAH, tool-calling, MMLU-Pro or GSM8K, and says it removes policy refusal but not grounded 'I can't' refusals. Exact removal (λ=1) is only partial (5/10, 7/10). The README argues the published baked checkpoint overshoots and inverts the direction (λ_eff≈2.43), which it blames for that checkpoint's degradation. The 'no second direction' claim concerns the residual of the weight edit, not refusal geometry.
record.recipe_differences: Runtime projection uses directions extracted by SVD from the difference between a base and an abliterated checkpoint, rather than the original harmful-minus-harmless activation-mean difference. The repo reports behavioral tests of the projection but does not claim to reproduce the original extraction recipe.
record.method_sensitivity: Refusal differs across λ: 9/10 at 0, 5/10 and 7/10 in two runs at 1, and 0/10 at 1.5 and 2. The README also reports that a short generation budget confounded quality measurements on this reasoning model.

fits_no_version.finding: SVD of the released abliteration edit: rank-1 energy 0.84–0.94. Rank-2 adds about 0.36 points. The residual is a flat tail attributed to FP8 requantization noise.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Released abliterated FP8 checkpoints carry about 10% non-directional requantization noise in the edit, beyond the intended rank-1 projection.

record.problems: The refusal test uses 10 low-harm triggers and classifies refusal from opening markers rather than reading response content. Benign controls are 4 prompts. The README says truthfulness suites hit a ceiling and do not discriminate; MMLU-Pro and GSM8K show no significant differences but are limited benchmarks. HumanEval was not run. Some quality results were initially confounded by short generation budgets, and the README warns that reasoning consumes 1,100–1,400 tokens before answers.
record.rows_left_out: Omitted runtime performance, latency, cache behavior, implementation/equivalence tests, extraction gates unrelated to the reported rank-1-versus-multiple-direction result, and other deployment details; they do not directly measure the claim's refusal behavior or the versions tested here.

untested.parts: Direction not extracted by harmful-minus-harmless mean activations. Adding the direction to induce refusal is not measured (λ<0 is allowed but untested). Only attention wo_b outputs are projected. HumanEval was not run.
No refusal rate is reported for the baked abliterated checkpoint.
No comparison of single vs multiple refusal directions in activations.
One reasoning model only. No non-reasoning comparison, and no analysis of the reasoning trace.

missing.what: Released baked abliterated checkpoint overshoots (λ_eff ≈2.43, inverting the direction to −143%). It degrades drafter acceptance (0.5128 vs 0.55 floor) and code throughput (46.6–55.3 vs 59.32 tok/s). This comes from a prior measurement in docs/projection-validation.md.
Truthfulness/sycophancy/false-premise suites score 100% at every λ up to 2.5 (0 yields in 113 opportunities), at ceiling.
Benign controls 0/4 falsely refused at λ=1 and λ=2.
Per-request λ end-to-end: 4/4 sealed triggers answered while the unsealed request still refused, in the same batch.
The 2048-token quality sweep showed apparent degradation (p=0.001), which the authors attribute to truncation from reasoning length. Conditional accuracy is flat across λ (93.6→95.1).

record.verdict_notes: The record's V4 'challenges' label is removed. The SVD analysis measures the rank of a third-party edit that was built rank-1, so it cannot test whether refusal is multi-directional. The record's V1 limits_scope partly cited limited capability coverage, which is untested scope, not limits_scope; it now rests only on λ=1 being partial. The refusal measure is weak: 10 low-harm triggers, opening-marker classification, and n=1–2 runs per λ.

versions.untested_parts: The direction was not found by harmful-minus-harmless mean activations; adding the direction to induce refusal on harmless requests was not tested. Capability coverage is limited to the reported retrieval, tool, truthfulness, and benchmark checks.
No reported refusal-rate test of a weight-edited released model.
The spectral analysis concerns checkpoint weight edits and their residuals, not direct comparisons of affine, cone, or multiple refusal-behavior directions.
The reported truthfulness checks do not measure a harmfulness judgment or its representation separately from refusal.
No cross-language, base-to-instruct, or cross-model-variant transfer test.
No comparison of refusal-training methods, data, or stages.
The README identifies the model as reasoning before answering but does not compare reasoning and non-reasoning models or test other reasoning models.

relation.reason: The study reports refusal rates under projection of the direction at λ = 0, 1, 1.5 and 2, plus benign controls and capability measures.

tranche.reason: A new setting (DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731, an MoE model that reasons before answering) with its own refusal rates across λ for removing a refusal direction, plus capability checks. The direction is recovered from a published abliteration's weight difference, so T2 is also defensible, but T3 is acceptable. It is not T4: the refusal-rate results bear directly on the claim.

source_check.notes: The direction is not a difference-in-means direction. It is 46 per-module unit vectors from the SVD of ΔW = W_abl − W_base of cebeuq/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-abliterated, applied only at the attention wo_b outputs. Refusal is n=10 low-harm triggers with an opening-marker classifier and no uncertainty. The pack gave no [lN] ids, so l1–l4 follow listing order.

statements.correction: ΔW = W_abl − W_base (abliterated minus base), SVD, one unit r̂ per edited module (46 attention wo_b modules). DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 reasons 1,100–1,400 tokens before answering. Refusal 9/10 → 0/10 at λ=1.5 and at λ=2 (10 low-harm triggers, opening-marker classifier, controls 0/4). Refusal counts have no uncertainty; t-tests on acceptance and McNemar p ≥ 0.09 on MMLU-Pro/GSM8K.
statements.problem: The statement says the direction comes from the SVD of the 'base-minus-abliterated' difference. The text computes ΔW = W_abl − W_base. The sign makes no difference to r̂r̂ᵀ, but the description is reversed. Also, the 'uncertainty' in the why-line covers acceptance, throughput and the MMLU-Pro/GSM8K tests, not the refusal counts. The statement is cut off in the pack, so only the part shown was checked.
No error. Caveat: 'exact removal' at λ=1 applies only at the 46 attention-output (wo_b) sublayers. MLP/MoE outputs and embeddings are untouched.
